doc_title: Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases
document_notes: Core theory source for heuristics, biases, representativeness, availability, base rates, risk perception, and confidence under uncertainty. Existing benchmark note: Broad positive recall judgment for heuristics, biases, and perceived risk.
manual_review_basis: benchmark target direct excerpt review where available

gold_section_refs.section_title: 1 Judgment under uncertainty: Heuristics and biases
gold_section_refs.notes: Classic overview of heuristics and biases; foundational theory about how people form beliefs under uncertainty—highly relevant for explaining heuristics, biases, and sources of miscalibrated decision confidence.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 2 Belief in the law of small numbers
gold_section_refs.notes: Discussion of the law of small numbers and overgeneralization from small samples — directly relevant to sampling biases and misplaced confidence in online decision contexts.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 3 Subjective probability: A judgment of representativeness
gold_section_refs.notes: Detailed treatment of subjective probability and representativeness heuristic — central for explaining probability distortions, confidence judgments, and misestimation of risk in online purchases.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 4 On the psychology of prediction
gold_section_refs.notes: Focused on representativeness with empirical studies and mechanisms; crucial empirical grounding for heuristics that affect decision confidence and perceived risk in complex product choices.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 6 Judgments of and by representativeness
gold_section_refs.notes: Kerntext zu Repräsentativitätsheuristik und zugehörigen Verzerrungen (Law of small numbers, Gambler’s fallacy). Direkt relevant für Entscheidungspsychologie, Heuristiken und deren Einfluss auf Entscheidungssicherheit und subjective probabil

gold_section_refs.section_title: 7 Popular induction: Information is not necessarily informative
gold_section_refs.notes: Kapitel zur Attributionstheorie (Kelley) und Schlussfolgerungsprozessen. Nützlich zur Erklärung kausaler Inferenzen, Attributionseffekte und deren Rolle bei Vertrauen/Unsicherheit in Kaufentscheidungen.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 8 Causal schemas in judgments under uncertainty
gold_section_refs.notes: Diskussion von kausalen Schemata und deren Einfluss auf Wahrscheinlichkeitsurteile. Hilfreich, um zu erklären, wie Nutzer Unsicherheit interpretieren und wie kausale Narrative Entscheidungssicherheit beeinflussen.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 9 Shortcomings in the attribution process: On the origins and maintenance of erroneous social assessments
gold_section_refs.notes: Analyse von Attributionsfehlern und deren Entstehung. Relevant für Verständnis von Fehleinschätzungen bei Produktbewertungen, Vertrauensbildung und der Persistenz falscher Eindrücke im Webshop-Kontext.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 10 Evidential impact of base rates
gold_section_refs.notes: Kernkapitel zu Basisratenvernachlässigung und Gewichtung spezifischer Evidenz. Sehr relevant für Informationsdarstellung, Vergleichbarkeit und wie Präsentationsformate Nutzerunsicherheit und Entscheidungssicherheit beeinflussen.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 11 Availability: A heuristic for judging frequency and probability
gold_section_refs.notes: Kerntext zur Availability-Heuristik: Mechanismen, Beispiele und Implikationen für Wahrscheinlichkeits- und Häufigkeitsschätzungen. Sehr relevant für Entscheidungsheuristiken, Vertrauen/Unsicherheit und wie Informationspräsentation Retrieval

gold_section_refs.section_title: 14 The simulation heuristic
gold_section_refs.notes: Einführung der Simulation‑Heuristik (mentale Konstruktion von Szenarien). Sehr relevant für Understanding von Entscheidungssicherheit, Erwartungsbildung und Gestaltung digitaler Informationspfade (z. B. Produktdemos, Szenarien).

gold_section_refs.section_title: 15 Informal covariation assessment: Data-based versus theory-based judgments
gold_section_refs.notes: Detailed treatment of covariation detection and informal inference is directly relevant to heuristics, updating beliefs under uncertainty, and how consumers infer product–outcome relationships (affects decision confidence and perceived risk

gold_section_refs.section_title: 16 The illusion of control
gold_section_refs.notes: Classic analysis of illusion of control explains a bias that inflates confidence and affects perceived controllability in purchase contexts (relevant for confidence, risk perception, and nudging safeguards).

gold_section_refs.section_title: 18 Probabilistic reasoning in clinical medicine: Problems and opportunities
gold_section_refs.notes: In-depth exploration of probabilistic reasoning under high-stakes uncertainty; highly applicable to online purchase decisions for complex products (diagnostics of signal interpretation, base-rate neglect, presentation of probabilities).

gold_section_refs.section_title: 19 Learning from experience and suboptimal rules in decision making
gold_section_refs.notes: Examines learning-from-experience and when heuristics persist — directly relevant to consumer learning, formation of decision rules, and design interventions to improve decision confidence and reduce biases.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 20 Overconfidence in case-study judgments
gold_section_refs.notes: Diskussion von Overconfidence und Angemessenheit von Vertrauen ist direkt relevant für «decision confidence» und Biases bei Kaufentscheidungen; liefert klassische Befunde und Beispiele für Überschätzung der Sicherheit.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 22 Calibration of probabilities: The state of the art to 1980
gold_section_refs.notes: Umfassende Übersichtsarbeit zur Kalibrierung von Wahrscheinlichkeiten (calibration) — zentral für Verständnis von Vertrauen/Confidence, Messung von Unsicherheit und Interventionen zur Verbesserung von Entscheidungsqualität.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 24 Evaluation of compound probabilities in sequential choice
gold_section_refs.notes: Experimentelle Befunde zu Fehleinschätzungen bei verketteten Wahrscheinlichkeiten (Addition statt Multiplikation). Relevante Einsicht für Gestaltung digitaler Entscheidungsprozesse und Informationsaufbereitung.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 25 Conservatism in human information processing
gold_section_refs.notes: Detailed classic account of conservatism in belief updating vs. Bayesian ideal. Highly relevant for explaining how consumers underweight new information, affecting decision confidence and uncertainty in online purchases.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 26 The best-guess hypothesis in multistage inference
gold_section_refs.notes: Multistage inference and the best-guess heuristic illuminate how sequential information (e.g., product reviews, specs) is integrated imperfectly, producing miscalibrated confidence — directly applicable to web-shop decision processes.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 27 Inferences of personal characteristics on the basis of information retrieved from one’s memory
gold_section_refs.notes: Bayesian modeling of inferences from noisy memory speaks to how consumers form attribute beliefs under retrieval uncertainty; useful for sections on perceived risk, information reliability, and design to reduce uncertainty.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 30 Intuitive prediction: Biases and corrective procedures
gold_section_refs.notes: Discusses intuitive prediction, role of singular vs. distributional information and limits of expert judgment — directly informs heuristics, biases, and how people form confidence under uncertainty; useful for explaining sources of miscalib

gold_section_refs.section_title: 31 Debiasing
gold_section_refs.notes: Focuses on debiasing and 'destructive testing' of behavioral phenomena — crucial for interventions, design of choice architectures and limits of corrective procedures relevant to decision confidence and ethical nudging.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 32 Improving inductive inference
gold_section_refs.notes: Addresses improving inductive inference with statistical heuristics and educative maxims — useful for practical measures to raise decision quality, presentable rules for users, and clear info design to reduce uncertainty.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 33 Facts versus fears: Understanding perceived risk
gold_section_refs.notes: Directly addresses perceived risk vs. objective facts and psychological elements of risk assessment and communication — highly relevant for perceived uncertainty in online purchases and design of trust-building information.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 34 On the study of statistical intuitions
gold_section_refs.notes: Detailed theoretical treatment of errors, biases, and statistical intuition—directly relevant to heuristics, biases, and dual-process considerations underlying decision confidence in uncertain online purchases.

gold_section_refs.section_title: 35 Variants of uncertainty
gold_section_refs.notes: Explicit discussion of different variants and phenomenology of uncertainty; useful for framing perceived risk/uncertainty, internal vs. external attributions, and modes of judgment in online buying contexts.
